Priya: Quick check — I'm seeing intermittent stalls where SSE streaming responses stop delivering chunks mid-JSON under load (50 concurrent clients). Repro is easy locally: high-QPS long responses. Any known SDK gotchas?

Alex: which SDK + runtime? Node fetch, Node SDK, or Python?

Priya: Node SDK + plain fetch both hit it, and I also repro with a tiny aiohttp client. Happens only under sustained concurrency (40–60 clients).

Jun: can you paste the minimal repro?

Priya: sure — node repro (simplified):
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8');
let tail = '';
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  const chunk = decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
  // accumulate until we parse a full JSON object
  tail += chunk;
  while (true) {
    const idx = tail.indexOf('
');
    if (idx === -1) break;
    const line = tail.slice(0, idx);
    tail = tail.slice(idx + 1);
    JSON.parse(line); // sometimes throws or blocks under load
  }
}
```
Python repro (aiohttp):
```py
async with session.get(url) as resp:
  decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
  async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(1024):
    s = decoder.decode(chunk)
    # split on newline and parse
```

Priya: behavior: one of two things under heavy load — parser raises UTF-8 error, or the client appears to hang (no more chunks) until the server times out.

Sam: fwiw, TextDecoder in Node needs { stream: true } to avoid throwing on split multibyte sequences; your code uses it though. If python incremental decoder is used incorrectly it can also drop bytes.

Marco: infra-bot run shows this pattern too — infra-bot: jenkins/stress-187 finished: 2 stalls, both on host gpu-dedicated-5, socket tx queues grew, kernel send buffers high. Attached tcpdump shows many small writes then a pause.

Alex: sounds like a backpressure deadlock between network read and our internal parser queue. If reader.read() is suspended because downstream queue is full and parser is CPU bound, under many clients you get lock-step stalls.

Priya: I tried increasing internal channel size to 1000 and the issue mostly disappeared (so it is related), but that's not a real fix.

Jun: Proposed SDK fix: 1) ensure read loop always drains socket into a small rotating buffer (so TCP window keeps moving), 2) hand off raw buffers to parser workers off the event loop (worker pool), 3) parser must be incremental and preserve trailing UTF-8 partial bytes between chunks. Add a unit test that intentionally splits multibyte sequences at every byte boundary.

Sam: sounds good. Also add a test that simulates slow parser (sleep in JSON parse) to verify we don't stall network readers.

Alex: design note — avoid unbounded worker pools; use backpressure signals to shed or fallback to a lighter parser (e.g., parse only top-level metadata and stream rest). But first patch should be safe: make reader non-blocking and decouple parse.

Priya: I'll open a PR with: incremental UTF-8 tolerant parser helper, a small worker-pool handoff, and two tests (byte-split multibyte, slow-parser load test). Will include Node and Python examples.

Sam: I'll review — ping me when draft PR exists :eyes:.

Jun: I'll run the stress harness on dedicated cluster once PR merges.

Priya: quick question for code review — for Node we used TextDecoder.decode(chunk, { stream: true }) which is correct, but we still saw a UTF-8 exception coming from JSON.parse on the assembled string. Any chance V8's string creation is throwing on truncated sequences even with stream true?

Alex: unlikely if stream:true used consistently. Could be a double-decode (buffer->string->buffer) happening in one codepath. Add extensive logging in the repro: log Buffer.byteLength(value) and tail.length before parse.

Marco: added a tiny tool to simulate extreme write bursts (attached) — infra-bot: ran it against canary; result: reproduced in 8/10 runs.

Priya: action items: (1) Priya: open PR with fixes + tests (ETA today EOD) ; (2) Sam & Alex: review PR (ETA tomorrow noon) ; (3) Jun: run stress harness after merge and report (ETA +24h) ; (4) Marco: keep the write-burst tool updated. :hammer_and_wrench:

infra-bot: noted — created ticket INF-2318 linking repro artifacts and jenkins logs.

Priya: thanks all — will post PR link here. If anyone has a quick pointer about V8 behaviour on partial utf8 I'd appreciate it. :pray:

Alex: also consider adding a canary config to Dedicated to run continuous streaming stress for 24h on new builds — catches regressions early. :shipit:

Sam: ack, will add checklist item to reviews for streaming edge cases.

Priya: PR opened:  https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js/pull/4823 (draft) — contains unit tests + small README on reproducer.

Sam: reviewing now.

Jun: kicked off stress once PR lands.

Priya: closing here for now, will update thread when tests finish. :white_check_mark:
